- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 0.5–1.5 points.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–3% or 0.5–1.5 points.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5 points to forecast to catch the dip.
- For 30-day horizon, if history shows volatility >10% over 5 days, model often over-smooths; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0 point to reflect uncertainty.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (or vice versa), model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment change within 2–3 days.
